answer: Core-periphery decomposition resists sybils: the trust graph is split into a densely interconnected honest core and a periphery, and influence requires genuine core membership — many reciprocal edges to other core nodes. A jetty of fakes attaches to the periphery but cannot manufacture the dense reciprocal interlinking of the core; its opal-smooth cluster stays peripheral however many internal edges it adds. The honest core is defined by mutual embedding no outside ring can fake, so sybils drift in the ocean of the periphery with near-zero weight.
